Package com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java

Class GryphonException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java.GryphonException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class GryphonException extends RuntimeException
The exception thrown by the Java facade when a Gryphon operation fails.

The facade exists so that Java users need not reach into the Scala API. Loading a graph was the one place where a failure made them: the bridge unwrapped a Scala Try with .get, which rethrows whatever the failure held — a com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.core.GraphException, a parse error, or anything else. The facade methods could only document that as RuntimeException, which tells a caller nothing they can act on. To tell "no such resource" from "the file parsed but describes an inconsistent graph", a Java caller had to catch RuntimeException and match on the message, or name a Scala class the facade otherwise hides. See issue #105.

That matters more since the graph-construction failures became carefully worded: a triplet carrying no attribute where the edge type cannot represent one, a triplet whose orientation disagrees with the graph being built, and an adjacency count that does not match the triplets each produce a message naming the offender and saying what to do about it. Those messages now reach a Java caller on an exception they can name.

It is unchecked, so no signature churn for callers who do not care, and the original throwable is always kept as the cause, so nothing that was available before is lost.

Note what this does not cover. The IllegalStateExceptions elsewhere in the facade — in MinimumSpanningTree, TopologicalSort, ShortestPaths, StronglyConnectedComponents and Graph — are precondition checks thrown before any Scala call is made. They report a caller's misuse of the facade rather than a failure inside Gryphon, which is a different thing, and they are left as they are.
